title: Choose Restock's visual world
question: The roll landed on the fridge-door list pad. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Fridge List Pad
options.lineage: the magnetic list pad every household keeps on the fridge
options.thesis: The household's oldest shared interface, kept for you: Restock writes the list and only leaves a note when it needs you.
options.viewport: Enamel ground; one canary sheet at the top holding the single decision that needs you; below it the pantry as a ruled list whose rule lines double as supply gauges; handled lines struck through in pencil with their reason.
options.risk: Tips into skeuomorphic kitsch if the paper gets texture, shadows, or handwriting fonts; it must stay flat, printed, and precise.

raised.raise: Supply is drawn in one ink at five densities; no traffic-light greens, ambers, or reds for stock levels.
Urgency is carried by line weight on the rule, not by added color.
When nothing needs you, the sheet is blank except one display-size line: Everything's stocked.
Zones are named for exactly what they are: Needs you, Pantry, Handled. No clever headers.
Every handled line carries its proof: the rule that allowed it.

options.label: The Countertop Appliance
options.lineage: 1960s German household appliance and calculator controls
options.thesis: Restock as a quiet appliance on the counter: few controls, precise scales, one indicator that lights only when it needs you.
options.viewport: A single housing: a dial-scale row per item showing days left, one orange-lit panel only when a decision waits, rules set on physical-looking sliders.
options.risk: Also the direction most calm product UIs land on; a knowing homage that can read familiar.

options.label: The Supply Board
options.thesis: The pantry as a departures board: every item a row ranked by days left, flaps clacking over when something is reordered.
options.viewport: A black board of item rows sorted by days left; rows that need you lit amber; a reorder flips the row's flaps to its new date.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on clarity: items ranked by days left read instantly. Loses on audience identification: a kitchen is not a concourse, and a full board risks the busy feel you ruled out.
options.risk: Reads as a transit gimmick, and constant flipping fights the calm default.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Stock levels as zones on an eleven-step tonal ramp.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets, each item a hatched zone.
options.case: Fuses poorly: households do not identify with darkroom notation, and hatching obscures a simple task.
options.kept: One tonal ramp carries all supply levels.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Items as stars, urgency as magnitude.
options.viewport: A chart of household items plotted by days left.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a pantry is not a sky; the metaphor costs clarity.
options.kept: Mark weight, not color, carries importance.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Words gather into weather as items run low.
options.case: Fuses poorly: motion-heavy and far from the task.
options.kept: One display-size sentence owns the calm state.

options.label: Stockroom Tags
options.thesis: Every zone labeled with its literal quoted name.
options.viewport: Label plates stacked like stenciled crates.
options.case: Fuses poorly: loud and ironic where the product should be calm and trusted.
options.kept: Zones named for exactly what they are.
options.risk: Fashion irony in a household tool.

options.label: Monochrome Proof
options.thesis: Every claim paired with the detail that proves it.
options.viewport: Claim, then proof, in a strict grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a marketing grammar, not a household tool.
options.kept: Every handled line carries its proof.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.viewport: A white list of items with thumbnails and a green action button, the arrangement every delivery app uses.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the delivery apps by design.
